cookies.intro: This Cookie Policy explains how {service} uses cookies and similar technologies when you visit our website. By continuing to use our site you agree to the use of cookies as described here.

s1.heading: 1. What are cookies?
s1.body: Cookies are small text files placed on your device by the websites you visit. They are widely used to make websites work, improve the user experience and provide information to the site owners.

s2.heading: 2. How we use cookies
s2.intro: We use the following types of cookies:

strictly.label: Strictly necessary cookies
strictly.text: These cookies are essential for the service to function — for example, to keep you signed in. They cannot be switched off.

analytics.label: Analytics cookies
analytics.text: With your consent, we use PostHog and Microsoft Clarity to understand how the product is used, measure page performance and improve the experience. These cookies store a persistent identifier so we can recognise returning visitors.

sessionReplay.label: Session replay cookies
sessionReplay.text: With your consent, Microsoft Clarity records interactions (clicks, scrolls, page navigation) so we can identify UX issues and fix them. Recordings are anonymised — we do not capture keystrokes in password fields.

s3.heading: 3. Anonymous analytics (no consent required)
s3.body: We also run PostHog in a cookieless, anonymous mode that does not store any cookies and does not use a persistent identifier across sessions. Because the data is fully anonymised, this processing runs without requiring your consent under the GDPR and the Italian Garante's guidelines.

s4.heading: 4. Managing your preferences
s4.body: You can change your cookie preferences at any time by clicking "Cookie preferences" in the footer of any page. You can also clear cookies through your browser settings. Note that blocking strictly-necessary cookies will prevent the service from working.

s5.heading: 5. Third-party cookies
s5.intro: Some cookies are placed by third-party services we use:

providers.name: Stripe
providers.purpose: Payment processing (only on the billing page)

s6.heading: 6. Changes to this policy
s6.body: We may update this Cookie Policy from time to time. When we do, we will revise the "Last updated" date above.

bestAiManager.q: What is the best AI social media manager for small businesses in 2026?
bestAiManager.a: Look for a tool that plans, writes, designs and publishes — not just schedules. Anomalia is built as an AI social media manager: it learns your brand from your website, proposes a weekly editorial plan, generates on-brand posts and articles, and publishes after you approve. That propose-approve loop keeps you in control while removing the day-to-day workload.

alternativesBuffer.q: What are good alternatives to Buffer or Hootsuite that also create the content?
alternativesBuffer.a: Buffer and Hootsuite are strong schedulers; they assume you already have captions and visuals. If you need creation as well as publishing, Anomalia is a fuller alternative: it generates captions, images and short video, builds the calendar, and can auto-publish to Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, Facebook, X and more. You still approve every post before it goes live.

aiVsHuman.q: Can AI replace a human social media manager?
aiVsHuman.a: For planning, drafting, designing and scheduling, yes — Anomalia covers the execution layer that usually costs €1,500–€5,000/month with a freelancer or agency. A human still wins on high-stakes brand judgment and live community crises. Anomalia is designed so you keep that judgment: nothing publishes without your approval, while the AI handles research, drafts and consistency.

howToChoose.q: How do I choose an AI social media autopilot?
howToChoose.a: Check four things: (1) does it learn your brand voice from real assets, not generic prompts; (2) can it create visuals, not only text; (3) do you approve before publish; (4) does it help beyond social — blog SEO and AI visibility (GEO). Anomalia scores on all four: Studio brand kit, image/video generation, propose-approve, plus blog articles and a GEO audit for ChatGPT/Perplexity citations.

onBrandAutopilot.q: Can AI post on Instagram and TikTok without sounding robotic?
onBrandAutopilot.a: Yes, if the system is grounded in your brand. Anomalia reads your website, products and guidelines, then writes captions tuned per platform. You can edit any draft. The goal is consistent, on-brand content at volume — not one-size-fits-all AI filler.

costVsAgency.q: How much does an AI social media manager cost compared to an agency?
costVsAgency.a: Agencies and freelancers commonly charge €1,500–€5,000+ per month for a handful of posts. Anomalia is priced per brand with plans from Go (prepare & export) through Pro (full autopilot with more posts, leads and radar sources). See current prices on the pricing page — typically a small fraction of agency retainers for more consistent output.

agencies.q: What is the best AI social media tool for agencies managing multiple brands?
agencies.a: You need multi-brand workspaces, per-brand voice, and billing that scales per client — not one shared calendar. Anomalia treats each brand as its own subscription with its own Studio, strategy and calendar, so agencies can run many clients without mixing voices or tools.

geoSeo.q: Which tools help you get cited by ChatGPT and Google, not just post on social?
geoSeo.a: Social reach alone does not win AI answers. You need crawlable pages, clear entity signals, and content that answers category questions. Anomalia pairs social autopilot with SEO/GEO: long-form articles, structured publishing, and a GEO audit that checks whether AI assistants can find and name your brand.
